author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Canadian supermarkets are changing labels and supply relationships as more shoppers seek domestic products and avoid U.S. goods amid a renewed trade dispute. Independent grocers are sourcing produce from Canada and countries including Mexico, Morocco, South Africa, Spain, Brazil and Honduras, according to retailers interviewed by Reuters.

Vince’s Market, which operates four stores in the Greater Toronto Area, said about 90% of its produce is now Canadian. The chain switched strawberry sourcing to Quebec and reduced advertising spending as the procurement changes increased operating pressure. Loblaw brought back large maple-leaf signs in fresh-food sections and reintroduced tags identifying products affected by tariffs. Metro said it would continue prioritizing Canadian goods.

The shift matters because Canada remains heavily dependent on imported fruits and vegetables. The United States supplies more than half of Canadian fresh-vegetable imports, although its share fell to 62.6% in July from 69% in July 2023. Ottawa is also planning about C$3 billion in spending on greenhouses and vertical farms over a decade, seeking to reduce seasonal supply constraints.
dek: Retailers are expanding origin labels and finding alternatives to U.S. produce as consumer preferences and trade tensions alter supply decisions.
headline: Canadian grocers shift sourcing as buy-local boycott reshapes shelves
